q: How do I calculate the CO2 from a process flare?
title: Process flare CO2 calculation
short: Measure the gas sent to the flare and its composition, then convert each carbon-bearing gas to CO2 by chemistry: one kilogram of methane burns to 2.75 kilograms of CO2. Report it as Scope 1, and report any unburnt methane separately with its global warming potential.
audience: Refineries, chemical plants, biogas and landfill gas operators

ul: Flow meter readings for the flare line.
Gas composition from lab analysis or an online analyser.
The flare efficiency your method uses, stated as an assumption.

p: Flaring fossil gas is Scope 1 fossil CO2. Flaring biogas or landfill gas releases biogenic CO2, reported outside the scopes, while unburnt methane from either still counts in Scope 1.
The pilot flame and purge gas burn all the time. Meter or estimate them and add them, since they run even when no process gas is flared.

example.title: Worked example: one month of flaring (illustrative inputs)
lines: Flare gas: 2,000 kg methane burnt in the month
Combustion: 1 kg CH4 burns to 44 / 16 = 2.75 kg CO2
Burnt at 98% (illustrative): 2,000 x 0.98 x 2.75 = 5,390 kg CO2
Unburnt methane: 2,000 x 0.02 = 40 kg CH4, reported separately with the AR6 GWP for fossil methane
example.note: Gas mass and efficiency are illustrative; use your flow meter, analysis and stated method.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 records. A per-unit figure divides those by the output you enter, and purchased materials are added from supplier data on the Scope 3 trail, labelled by source.
